signals.title: NZD/USD — G10 Bilateral Theme + Geopolitical Headwinds
signals.text: NZD 1W avg +1.252% (n=4) vs USD -1.315% (n=7) establishes a 2.567% spread that faces a Monday open tests as Iran/Iraq transit developments shift the geopolitical risk-premium. While NZD maintains the strongest G10 momentum, its accommodative real rate of -1.56% and extreme COT short -27.4k (pctl 15) suggest the rally is a short-covering squeeze vulnerable to deteriorating risk sentiment. The RBNZ meeting on 2 September remains the primary policy anchor for this trend. Trade bias: Bullish NZD/USD into the open; momentum favors continuation but geopolitical escalation caps the upside. Catalyst: Sydney open. Risk: Sharp risk-off reversal if Strait of Hormuz tensions escalate further.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Crowded Short Reversal + Retail Extreme
signals.text: AUD COT LF long +49.7k (75.2% long) alongside extreme retail sentiment (90% short) sets up a high-conviction contrarian continuation bias toward the 0.7200 handle. The -72bp OIS carry advantage for AUD and a resilient UK/AU growth outlook support the bid despite a moderate negative ESI of -10.3. The next RBA meeting (mkt: 100% hold priced) on 29 September determines if the current hold stance can withstand the building momentum. Trade bias: Long AUD/USD; retail extreme short positioning (90%) suggests further upside via contrarian flow. Catalyst: Sydney open. Risk: Break below SMA200 at 0.6954 invalidates the bullish structure.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry Advantage vs Put Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY closed at 158.94 with a +265bp OIS carry advantage that faces heavy resistance from a strong -1.96 options risk reversal put skew. JPY COT net short -73.6k remains a significant squeeze risk, especially as USD data persistence (ESI -15.1) and a Bear Steepener yield regime (2s10s +55bp) pressure the dollar's yield dominance. The next BoJ meeting (mkt: 65% hike priced) on 18 September is the catalyst for resolving the widening policy divergence. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY; strong options put skew (-1.96) indicates heavy hedging for a JPY recovery. Catalyst: Tokyo open. Risk: US 10Y yield surge above 4.80% reinforces the carry trade.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Positioning Risk + Real Rate Advantage
signals.text: GBP COT LF long +46.1k (pctl 94) represents a crowded-long risk as the pair trades above all major SMAs (20/50/200) following a 1.17% weekly gain. A restrictive real rate of +0.85% provides fundamental support, though retail sentiment is now heavily skewed with 83% of traders short. The BoE meeting on 17 September will clarify if the current yield support can offset the negative ESI trend of -8.0. Trade bias: Neutral/Bullish; crowded COT longs (pctl 94) limit immediate upside despite positive real rates. Catalyst: London open. Risk: Sustained close below SMA200 at 1.3427.

signals.title: USD/CAD — Negative ESI + Short Squeeze Setup
signals.text: USD/CAD closed Friday at 1.3763, pressured by a strong positive Canadian ESI (+24.9) and a massive CAD COT net short of -89.8k (pctl 13). The +138bp OIS carry advantage for USD remains the primary floor, but persistent USD data misses (ESI -15.1) favor further CAD outperformance toward the SMA200 at 1.3843. The BoC meeting on 9 September determines if the data-driven CAD strength is sustainable. Trade bias: Bearish USD/CAD; extreme CAD COT shorts (pctl 13) create high potential for a recovery squeeze. Catalyst: Sydney open. Risk: WTI oil falling below $85/bbl.
